title: Two Integration Boost Instances inherit their near-term qualification from the wrong sibling primitive
content:
Every Instance's Routine Protocol inherits the same base class — "A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1 - Routine Protocol" — but qualifies it with a near-term process, and within the Integration Boost primitive the qualifications diverge.

Curve (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.2.2.2.1) and Morpho (…3.2.1) point at "A.2.2.9.**2**.2.1.3.2.1 - Near Term Process" — a document under A.2.2.9.2, the Integration Boost Primitive. Euler (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.2.1.2.1) and the prospective Compound Instance (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.4.1.3.1) point instead at "A.2.2.9.**1**.2.1.3.3.1 - Near-Term Process" — a document under A.2.2.9.1, the *Distribution Reward* Primitive, which is the citation every Distribution Reward Instance uses.

This is not cosmetic. Inheritance is load-bearing in this Artifact: A.6.1.1.4.2.5.2.2.1.2.1 states that modifications to inherited logic "automatically propagate to this Instance," and no Instance declares any customization. The qualification document therefore determines what operational logic actually applies. Under a literal reading, Euler and Compound are qualified by another primitive's transitional process while Curve and Morpho are qualified by their own.

The likeliest explanation is that Instances were drafted by copying a Distribution Reward Instance and two of the four citations were never repointed. But because inheritance propagates silently and the Instances cannot override it, a mis-cited qualifier is exactly the kind of defect that changes behaviour without appearing in any diff of Skybase's own decisions — and correcting it requires a Root Edit, since these are `[Core]` documents.
description: Euler and Compound cite the Distribution Reward near-term process A.2.2.9.1.2.1.3.3.1, while Curve and Morpho cite the Integration Boost one at A.2.2.9.2.2.1.3.2.1.
